messages.author: 8aa9b8cc06fdc99c
messages.subject: problems with corr_matrix positive definiteness (test?)
parts:
Following up on Marcel Jonker's problems, I found this
very simple model that breaks:

parameters {
corr_matrix[100] Omega;
}
transformed parameters {
corr_matrix[100] Omega3;

Omega3 <- Omega;
for (i in 1:100) for (j in 1:100) Omega3[i,j] <- Omega3[j,i];
}
model {
}

I'm seeing the same error as Marcel:

-------------
~/temp2/jonker$ ./boo --iter=100
Exception: Invalid value of Omega3: Error in function validate transformed params d: y is not positive definite. y(0,0)
is 1.
Diagnostic information:
Dynamic exception type: std::domain_error
std::exception::what: Invalid value of Omega3: Error in function validate transformed params d: y is not positive
definite. y(0,0) is 1.
-----------------

If I provide command-line option:

--init=0

it will sample. So it seems to be initial-value sensitive.

It may just be the test for positive definiteness that's broken.
It'd be great if someone better than me at the multivariate
operations took a look.

- Bob

I don't think the test is broken, per se. Any positive definite matrix can be sufficiently close to singular that it fails a numerical test with some positive epsilon. What doesn't make sense is why the whole thing comes to a halt instead of just rejecting the proposal.

Ben
